content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: shift breaks, add IVR callbacks and an outage message at no extra cost, lifting service level to 85.5% for 11:30-13:30","why":"The payments spike is caused by the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998). upi_payment_failed calls are running at 2.56x normal. Staffing and handle time are not the problem. Doing nothing (P0) only just reaches the 80% target at 80.4%, and general would sit at 71.6%. P1 costs nothing and follows policy. It lifts the disruption-window service level to 85.5%, with payments at 90.2% and general at 78.1%. Abandons fall from 4.8% to 3.5%, and the rest of the day rises to 93.7%. It works by delaying 12:00-12:30 breaks, offering callbacks on both queues and playing an outage message for UPI-failure and payment-status callers.","trade_offs":["General stays below 80% (78.1%) under P1. The overall figure is carried by payments at 90.2%.","P2 costs ₹720 and gets general to 84.5%, with an overall service level of 89.4% and abandons of 2.9%. It relies on chat deflection.","P3 costs ₹4,320 for 20 agent-hours of overtime and is the strongest plan: 92.5% overall, 88.3% on general and 1.7% abandons.","P1 depends on agents accepting delayed breaks and on customers taking callbacks. Callbacks returned later add load after the window."],"watch":"Watch general queue service level through 12:00-13:00, and whether the UPI incident is resolved by 13:30. If general falls well below 78% or the outage runs on, move to P2 (₹720) or P3."}
